subject: Pilot extension options and bridge pricing
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-14T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot extension options and bridge pricing

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To summarize next-step options for Aurelia's 30-day pilot: we can either (A) extend the existing timebox by 4 weeks with a modest extension fee, or (B) leave the end date and add credits to cover the additional test volume. High-level numbers below so you have something to share with Procurement quickly: 

- Option A — 4-week extension: flat fee $12,000 (covers sustained concurrency up to current pilot SLA, includes 1 additional engineering office hour per week during the extension)
- Option B — Credit top-up: $18,000 in token credits applied to the current pilot account; no additional engineering hours included

Concessions we can consider if you want a lower headline price: a 20% discount on Option A in exchange for written commitment to a post-pilot evaluation call and a short case study should the pilot meet the success criteria. Alternatively, we can split the difference and do $10,000 + 5k professional services credit (for integration time).

Two asks from our side to make this fast for Procurement: 1) confirm which option Procurement prefers (A or B) and 2) whether legal needs a short amendment or a formal addendum. I can get a one-page amendment prepared today.

I attached a draft one-page amendment and a short SOW with the engineering hours outline.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min call to walk through.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park

Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick summary. Procurement is asking whether you can do Option A for $9,000 with the commitment clause (case study + evaluation call) — they flagged budget constraints for Q3. Two questions from legal/procurement:

1) Can Redwood confirm there will be no change to data handling or retention during the extension (we have an upcoming internal audit)?
2) If we proceed with the $9k concession, can you add a short SLA language that keeps latency/uptime the same as the pilot?

If you can get us a signed amendment that addresses the two bullets above, Procurement will fast-track. Otherwise they want to see a signed SOW and the exact invoice terms.

Thanks — I’m looping Procurement on this thread.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Data & AI, Aurelia Health

Kim —

Quick internal note on concessions we can make without involving Finance beyond a standard approval:

- Approve Option A at $9,000 (25% off) if the customer signs a short amendment and commits to an evaluation call + permission for a 1-paragraph use case quote (not a full case study) within 60 days of pilot close.
- Add 5k of PS (professional services) credit to cover any integration troubleshooting during the extension (we can consume against CS hours).
- For the SLA ask: confirm we can mirror the pilot SLA (no change to retention or data handling) — engineering already confirmed there’s no policy change for the extension window. We should explicitly call out retention in the amendment: "No change to data retention or processing during the extension period."

I attached an updated amendment with retention and SLA language baked in. If Priyom or Kim approve, I can send to Sarah with a DocuSign link.

—David
